summary:
Trends is the category to trust right now across every rating — all four models show an identical 14-day 8-3 (73%, n=11) trends read riding a 4-game win streak, a stark reversal from the ice-cold SP and bullpen numbers (36% at 4-7, n=11 each, with bullpen on a 3-game losing streak). That split matters because trends+sp combos still hit 57.8% (367-268, n=635) over the full season — the market's best agreeing pair — but with SP currently frozen, the trends signal is doing the heavy lifting. Hitting is also running warm at 64% (7-4, n=11) across R1-R3, giving a second category worth leaning on when it stacks with trends.

Today's lone game is about as clean as the slate gets: TBR @ MIL, and all four ratings converge hard on MIL, with deltas ranging from R3's +1.33 to R2's +1.64 — full consensus, no fade signal anywhere. That's a big deal given MIL's standing profile when picked: 47-22 (68%, n=69) on the season and a blistering 26-12 (68%, +17.0u) in strong-play spots. Facing Jacob Misiorowski against Nick Martinez, MIL projects well both on raw model strength and on the trends-category tailwind that's hot across the board. R2 stands out as the rating to size up here — it's the only one showing positive unit P/L in every window (7d +1.0u, 14d +1.0u, 30d +7.0u, season +79.0u) and carries the strongest MIL delta at +1.64. R1 and R3, by contrast, are nursing short-term strong-play dips (R1 14d -1.0u, R3 14d -1.0u) despite healthy season marks, so don't overweight their confidence today beyond the consensus signal. With SP and bullpen both cold, the case for MIL here leans on trends/hitting strength and R2's hot hand rather than pitching-matchup categories — bet the consensus, size through R2.
